Harper Lin: FYI we just got a private deploy report: customer 'Aegis Research' found a potential token-reuse issue in keystore-proxy when combined with older kube-proxy netpols. Could be a vuln chain.
Diego Morales: details? reproducible?
Harper Lin: they ran a red-team smoke and observed that a rotated ephemeral token could be replayed for ~45s against the proxy on a different pod if the old token wasn't immediately revoked. We think it's an off-by-one TTL handling in the proxy's token cache.
sec-bot: Alert tag: VULN-POTENTIAL-176980. Collected artifacts: keystore-proxy version=3.4.1, k8s-netpol=1.22, private-deploy-onprem.
Diego Morales: logs?
Harper Lin: sanitized log excerpt:
```
2026-03-12T10:00:12Z keystore-proxy INFO token=svcacct-aegis-xyz validated ttl=30s cached_until=10:00:57Z
2026-03-12T10:00:58Z keystore-proxy WARN token=svcacct-aegis-xyz replay_detected? allowed_by_cache
```
Oncall Ops: netpols in that cluster use a permissive intra-namespace rule (we recommended deny-by-default but customer had legacy allow). Replay was possible because network path to another pod wasn't blocked.
Ellen Wright: so two issues: proxy cache TTL handling + network isolation gap. Attack vector requires compromised token source. Impact: if attacker obtained token they could briefly use it across pods to request decrypts during window.
Diego Morales: immediate mitigation: 1) publish hotfix to keystore-proxy to invalidate cache entries on token rotation events and tighten TTL floor, 2) recommend customers apply netpol deny-by-default for keystore-proxy, 3) add SIEM rule to flag replayed token patterns (same token used from two distinct pod IPs within TTL).
Harper Lin: agreed. For on-prem customers we can push a config patch: `TOKEN_CACHE_SAFE_TTL=5s` default for private deploys until hotfix is out. Also provide a kubectl netpol snippet to lock intra-namespace egress: `egress: - to: {podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: hsm-connector}}}`.
sec-bot: Security classification: MEDIUM. Recommended CVSS draft pending triage. Created ticket INF-9001 (proxy-cache-hotfix) and INF-9002 (netpol-hardening-guidance).
Oncall Ops: mitigation steps executed for Aegis Research: set TOKEN_CACHE_SAFE_TTL=5s on keystore-proxy, applied restrictive netpol for keystore-proxy pods, rotated affected service tokens, and replay detection rule enabled in SIEM. Customer reported no exfil observed.
Diego Morales: follow-ups: 1) vuln triage: run PR advisory, coordinate CVE if confirmed, 2) add preflight check for private deploy: token-rotation-event hook that invalidates proxies' caches, 3) audit: export decrypt call logs for last 24h and sign bundle for customer compliance.
Ellen Wright: compliance note: ensure we capture signed timestamped artifact showing when keys/tokens rotated and that we forced cache invalidation. Also draft customer communication: transparent, include mitigation and ETA for hotfix (48h).
Harper Lin: I'll lead the hotfix and patch notes. Diego, can you own customer comms and compliance artifacts?
Diego Morales: on it. Draft will state: root cause, mitigations applied, commands we ran, and offer for signed attestation.
sec-bot: Reminder: add e2e test to infra-agent suite to simulate token rotations + netpol variations and assert no replay through proxy cache.
Harper Lin: thanks. Closing loop: INF-9001/9002 created, hotfix branch opened, will roll to private deploy customers with a coordinated patch schedule. Posting postmortem when done. :thumbsup:
